dubious_claims: outcomeLine says you can 'read any Spanish word aloud', but c/z, soft g, qu/gu, v/b and x are never taught
Try-it message 'Every letter you see makes its sound' is false: the u in que/guerra is silent
gracias as 'GRAH-see-as' is Latin American seseo, while a Madrid waiter would typically say 'GRAH-thee-as'; this is unflagged in a Madrid scene

json.why: Card 1 opens with a flat textbook claim and holds only a vowel chart with sound-alike words, no real image.

dubious_claims: 'Gracias' is given as GRAH-see-as in a Madrid scene, but in Madrid the c before i is usually 'th' (GRAH-thee-as).
The outcomeLine says 'read any Spanish word aloud', which overclaims: the chapter never covers c/g before e/i, qu, or gu.
The chapter has no exercises and no feedback, so checks 4-6 cannot pass.

json.fix: Open card 1 with a café moment, such as Kabir reading 'jamón' off a Madrid menu and saying it right on the first try, then show the though/through/tough contrast.
json.why: The opener is a flat textbook claim, and the card is a list of sound comparisons with no scene, so a reader with no interest scrolls past before Kabir appears.

dubious_claims: Outcome line and card 1 say you can read any or nearly any word, but c, z, g, qu, v/b, y and single r are never taught, so 'any' is an overclaim.

Title 'Ten sounds' does not match the material: the chapter teaches five vowels plus five letter rules, and 'ten sounds' is not enough to read any word.
json.fix: Open with a concrete moment, e.g. 'In Madrid you can read a menu aloud on day one; in London, "though", "through" and "tough" still trip up natives.' Retitle the card to drop the 'any word' promise.
json.why: It opens with a flat textbook statement, uses word examples instead of a real image, and promises ten sounds for any word, which the chapter can't deliver.
